metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Safeguard E POSITIVE pole, authoritarian variant: did high oil/gas rents buy regime SURVIVAL through the 2011 Arab Spring while non-rentier MENA states (Tunisia/Egypt/Libya, case04) destabilized? Tests whether rent-funded distribution + co-optation predicts stability despite low voice -- a positive E outcome carried with a LATENT reversal-risk flag (the bargain is contingent on sustained rents). Pre-P1 gap (~0.115) clears the Mod4 ~0.10 margin, so an ordinal read is permitted.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; both entities carry real MI v2 re-scores. Stress event = the 2011 Arab Spring; scored ~2010 (pre) vs 2024. The authoritarian rentier counterpart to Botswana's democratic rent-stabilization (case38) and the negative pole Venezuela (case22); contrasts with the non-rentier Arab Spring case (case04).

pre_event.event_description: On the eve of the 2011 Arab Spring, two high-rent Gulf monarchies face the same regional wave that toppled or convulsed non-rentier governments in Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, Yemen and Syria. Both deploy the rentier bargain -- large fiscal packages, public-sector wage and benefit increases, and subsidies -- alongside security measures to pre-empt mass mobilization.

context.neighbor_details: Regional turbulence (Yemen to the south; Arab Spring contagion) but no state-threatening neighbor.

Saudi Arabia.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Saudi Arabia: high oil rents (~24% of GDP, World Bank 2021 vintage) fund a distributive authoritarian bargain. Pre-2010 P1 driven by effectiveness/order with very low voice -- the rentier-authoritarian configuration. Safeguard E POSITIVE pole conditioned on rent-funded co-optation.

United Arab Emirates.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. UAE: hydrocarbon rents (~16% of GDP, World Bank 2021 vintage) plus a diversified emirate economy fund a high-effectiveness, low-voice federation of emirates. Strong government-effectiveness and order scores; the rentier-authoritarian bargain with greater diversification than Saudi Arabia.

a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Either monarchy is overthrown/collapses around 2011, OR the ordering reverses on outcome (Saudi > UAE on post-MI).

Saudi Arabia.outcome_summary: Regime survival as predicted. The 2011 wave was absorbed via large fiscal packages and security measures; no regime change. P1 rose 0.532 -> 0.631 and MI rose 0.623 -> 0.693 (Tier 2 throughout), reflecting effectiveness/order gains and post-2016 Vision-2030 state-capacity investment under continued low voice. The positive Safeguard E (authoritarian variant) outcome -- with the latent reversal-risk flag intact (stability remains rent-contingent).

no regime change through the Arab Spring
post-2016 Vision 2030 state-capacity drive; sustained low voice

analysis.overall_assessment: Confirmation: high rents bought regime survival through the 2011 Arab Spring in both monarchies while non-rentier MENA (case04) destabilized. The positive Safeguard E (authoritarian variant) outcome is recorded WITH a standing latent reversal-risk flag, because the stability is rent-contingent rather than institution-anchored.
safeguards_triggered: E (resource rents -- POSITIVE pole, authoritarian variant)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Safeguard E's positive pole operates under authoritarianism, not only under good institutions (Botswana, case38): rent-funded distribution + co-optation can purchase regime survival through a region-wide shock despite very low voice -- but the framework must carry a LATENT reversal-risk flag, because the stability is contingent on sustained rents rather than on accountable institutions. It is the rentier MIRROR of the non-rentier Arab Spring collapses (case04) and the positive pole opposite Venezuela's rentier capture (case22).
analysis.baseline_impact: None; adds two MENA cases, the second/third rent-stabilization exemplars (authoritarian variant, with Botswana case38), and the rentier counterfactual to the Arab Spring case (case04).
